description:
NASA-level tools. Everyday words.

The satellites saw it all. Nobody told the story.

Ask a question about a place in your own words. Alibi picks the NASA records that can answer it, tests whether the change is real, and tells you in plain English what is real and what is only a clue.
summary:
Alibi is an AI-powered Earth science investigation platform that turns everyday questions into scientific discoveries using real NASA satellite data.

Through an interactive 3D globe, users can select any location on Earth, investigate environmental changes and explore historical trends through interactive maps, visualisations and easy-to-understand explanations.

Unlike traditional data visualisation tools, Alibi acts as a scientific detective: it automatically finds relevant datasets, performs statistical analyses to detect significant environmental trends and explores potential relationships between climate variables. Every finding is backed by real calculations, with uncertainty clearly communicated and correlation never mistaken for causation.

By making complex Earth observation data accessible to everyone, Alibi bridges the gap between satellite science and everyday understanding. It empowers citizens, students and researchers to explore our changing planet, uncover environmental patterns and make more informed decisions about Earth's future.
details:
Alibi – NASA-level tools. Everyday words.

Alibi is an interactive Earth science investigation platform that transforms natural-language questions into evidence-based investigations using real NASA Earth observation data. Users can select a location on an interactive 3D globe and ask questions about environmental changes in their own words. Alibi automatically identifies relevant satellite datasets, analyses historical trends, compares potential climate drivers and presents its findings through interactive maps, visualisations and clear, accessible explanations.

Going beyond simple data visualisation, Alibi combines statistical rigour with AI-powered investigation. It uses methods such as the Mann–Kendall trend test, Sen’s slope and false discovery rate correction to determine whether environmental changes are statistically significant, how fast they are occurring and whether measured climate factors may help explain them. Crucially, AI never calculates statistics or decides scientific conclusions: every numerical claim is validated against computed results, uncertainty is explicitly communicated, and correlation is never presented as proof of causation.

Built with Python, FastAPI, LangGraph, Next.js, React, MapLibre and 3D visualisation technologies, the platform integrates datasets from NASA missions and services including GRACE/GRACE-FO, MODIS, GLDAS, NASA POWER and NASA GIBS, alongside clearly attributed complementary sources.

Its innovative detective-inspired approach makes complex Earth science accessible to everyone, from researchers and students to citizens and decision-makers. Through real-world investigations involving Lake Mead, the Aletsch Glacier, Doñana wetlands and the Great Barrier Reef, Alibi demonstrates how satellite observations can reveal environmental changes and help distinguish climate-related signals from other possible influences.

Our goal is to bridge the gap between scientific data and public understanding, empowering people to explore Earth's changing systems, question what they observe and make better-informed decisions through transparent, reproducible and accessible science.
